Insights

Adapting positioning and pricing for the Saudi market

Practical considerations for aligning your value proposition and price architecture with Saudi customers.

Many international businesses assume that a proposition that works elsewhere will transfer unchanged. In practice, customer priorities, competitive reference prices and channel economics differ, and the gap shows up quickly in sales conversion and margin.

01

Start from the customer, not the price list

Identify the segments you want to win and what they value most: quality, service, brand, speed or relationship. Pricing should reflect that value, not simply convert a global rate card.

02

Benchmark local reference prices

Customers anchor on what comparable local and international offers cost. Understand those anchors, including discounts and payment terms, before setting your own.

03

Account for total cost to serve

Import duties, logistics, localisation, partner margins and after-sales support all affect the price you can sustain. Build these into your model early.

04

Test, learn and adjust

Start with a focused pilot, monitor conversion and feedback, and refine positioning and price before scaling.

Conclusion

Positioning and pricing are not one-off decisions. Treat them as hypotheses to test in market, with clear measures for what success looks like.
